name: Mare Tranquillitatis Pit
mission: Candidate lava-tube entrance · proposed target of the Moon Diver mission concept
pit_size: 100 × 88 m opening, ~105 m deep, overhangs of 10–15 m
notes: Vertical-walled pit in mare basalt, the type example of lunar pits. Its shadowed floor is modelled to stay near +17 °C.

extra.Pit (LROC catalog): 100 × 88 m opening, ~105 m deep, overhangs of 10–15 m

notes_subsurface.claim: The shadowed part of the Mare Tranquillitatis pit stays near +17 °C through the lunar day, while the sunlit surface swings by roughly 290 K.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Modelled from Diviner data; the cave behind the pit has not been observed thermally.
notes_subsurface.source: Horvath, Paige & Hayne (2022), Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2022GL099710

notes_subsurface.claim: The LROC catalog lists 278 lunar pits: 16 in mare basalt, 5 in highlands and 257 in impact melt. Several mare pits show overhangs that may open into lava tubes.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Counts from the current LROC catalog version.
notes_subsurface.source: LROC Lunar Pit Locations catalog (Wagner & Robinson)

notes_subsurface.claim: Seven candidate cave skylights were found on the flanks of Arsia Mons, Mars, with minimum depths of about 68–130 m.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Depths are minimum values from THEMIS thermal and visible images.
notes_subsurface.source: Cushing et al. (2007), Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2007GL030709

notes_subsurface.claim: The bacterium Sphingomonas desiccabilis increased rare earth element leaching from basalt on the ISS (BioRock), in microgravity and simulated Mars gravity.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Terrestrial basalt, small samples, 21 days. The report's “+429 %” and yields per 100 kg are not in the paper.
notes_subsurface.source: Cockell et al. (2020), Nature Communications 11, 5523

notes_subsurface.claim: Lunar surface missions are COSPAR Category II: IIb for the poles and permanently shadowed regions, IIa elsewhere. Category IV applies to Mars landers.
notes_subsurface.caveat: The team report lists lunar caves as Category IV, which is incorrect.
notes_subsurface.source: COSPAR Panel on Planetary Protection, 2021 update

notes_subsurface.claim: 15 m of rock attenuates ionizing radiation by 99.8 %.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Plausible order of magnitude; needs a transport calculation or citation.
notes_subsurface.source: Team report

notes_subsurface.claim: Bacillus subtilis spores and Deinococcus radiodurans keep over 99.5 % viability for 30 days inside a lava tube.
notes_subsurface.caveat: Described as a simulation result; model and inputs not documented.
notes_subsurface.source: Team report
